ON.name: Ontario
ON.summary: Home Renovation Savings (Enbridge Gas + Save on Energy) is the only province-wide rebate. The assessment path covers insulation, windows, doors, air sealing, heat pump water heaters and the assessment itself, but its follow-up assessment must be done by December 31, 2026. The no-assessment path covers heat pumps, attic insulation (participating contractors only) and smart thermostats.

attic.conditions: Initial EnerGuide assessment before any work, at least two recommended upgrades, then a follow-up assessment with the same service organization. cityCaveats.kitchener: Most Kitchener homes buy natural gas from Kitchener Utilities, not Enbridge. Home Renovation Savings' assessment-path terms define eligible gas homes as those heated with "Enbridge-supplied natural gas" and other homes as heated by oil, propane, wood or electricity, so a Kitchener Utilities gas-heated home fits neither group; confirm with the program before planning around it. Kitchener Utilities offers its own $75 smart thermostat bill credit. RetrofitWR loans are limited to GrandBridge Energy customers.
cityCaveats.kingston: Central Kingston gas customers buy from Utilities Kingston, not Enbridge, so the same Home Renovation Savings eligibility gap applies. Kingston filled it with Better Homes Kingston rebates for Utilities Kingston gas customers, but that program is no longer accepting applications (waitlist).

QC.summary: Rénoclimat changed on October 1, 2026: the evaluation is now optional, insulation is paid per square foot with house caps, windows must be ENERGY STAR Most Efficient ($300 each), and doors, air sealing and HRVs dropped out. Heat pumps are Hydro-Québec LogisVert's territory (no audit). Hydro-Québec's roof insulation + caulking grant ($1,500) is still listed for electrically heated houses.

BC.summary: Market-rate rebates come from the Home Renovation Rebate Program. Insulation, windows and doors are open to most heating fuels. In our 13 BC cities, heat pump rebates are mainly for electrically heated homes; FortisBC gas customers can get $4,000 for a dual-fuel system (a heat pump paired with a gas furnace, replacing a furnace at least 15 years old), and full switches from gas, propane or oil are paid only in northern BC (100 Mile House and north) unless the household is income-qualified. The requirements changed for invoices dated on or after October 15, 2026, so confirm amounts before you buy.

airSealing.conditions: Homes built before 2014, done with an eligible attic insulation upgrade by a TakeCharge-approved installer; paid to the installer.

ashp.program: takeCHARGE Oil to Electric Incentive Program
ashp.amount: General: Central Heat Pump save up to $9,000; Multiple Mini-Split or Multi-Split Heat Pump save up to $6,500; Electric Furnace/Boiler save up to $5,000. Income-Qualified: up to $22,000 / $18,000 / $10,000. "Incentives can cover up to 100% of the cost of switching from oil to electricity."
ashp.conditions: Homes heated by oil (at least 500 L in a 12-month period) or propane (at least 1,000 L); owner; permanent foundation, primary residence, on the island or Labrador interconnected grid; new homes excluded. Whole-home heating with heat pumps on NRCan's OHPA list; backup heat required. Participating installer, paid directly; oil tank removed; pre-approval holds funds for 365 days; projects completed after April 1, 2023. Income-qualified heat pump participants also get NRCan's…
ashp.deadline: "The Oil to Electric Program is still accepting applications." No closure date set; install within 365 days of pre-approval.

measureNotes.ashp: Electrically heated homes adding a heat pump get on-bill financing, not a rebate.
measureNotes.gshp: Oil to Electric covers air source heat pumps (and electric furnaces/boilers), not ground source.
measureNotes.thermostat: The Mysa thermostat pilot (Newfoundland Power) is closed to enrolment; no purchase rebate.
measureNotes.assessment: No evaluation subsidy; takeCHARGE lists four companies offering assessments.

YT.name: Yukon
YT.summary: Yukon's Energy Branch pays some of the largest per-home amounts in Canada: insulation up to $12,000 for walls, $5,000 for air sealing to a tight target, and 50% of heat pump costs up to $10,500 (100% up to $24,000 for low-to-median incomes).

attic.program: Yukon home insulation and air sealing rebate
attic.amount: $2,500 for insulating your attic (proportional to the percentage of attic surface area insulated).
attic.basis: Full amount when 100% of the attic goes from R-40 or less to R-60+; scale by share of area.
attic.conditions: Existing residence (5 years or older). Energy assessment with an NRCan-registered advisor before applying and a follow-up assessment after the work ($50 each at the reduced fee), with a new assessment after each stage if done in stages. Receipts within 1 year of applying; rebate within 12 weeks. Attic must be R40 or less before and reach R60 or more.
attic.deadline: Receipts dated within 1 year of applying.

walls.program: Yukon home insulation and air sealing rebate
walls.amount: Up to $12,000 for insulating above-ground walls (based on the percentage of the total wall area insulated).
walls.basis: Full amount only if all above-ground walls are insulated and the R-value at least doubles; scale by share of wall area.
walls.conditions: Existing residence (5 years or older). Energy assessment with an NRCan-registered advisor before applying and a follow-up assessment after the work ($50 each at the reduced fee), with a new assessment after each stage if done in stages. Receipts within 1 year of applying; rebate within 12 weeks. Must at least double the existing R-value.
walls.deadline: Receipts dated within 1 year of applying.

basement.program: Yukon home insulation and air sealing rebate
basement.amount: Up to $10,000 for insulating below-ground walls (proportional to the depth; maximum at 6 feet or more). $2,000 for insulating slabs or floor systems.
basement.basis: Full amount for below-grade walls 6 ft deep or more; the Energy Branch summary page says up to $12,000, the detailed page $10,000 (we used $10,000).
basement.conditions: Existing residence (5 years or older). Energy assessment with an NRCan-registered advisor before applying and a follow-up assessment after the work ($50 each at the reduced fee), with a new assessment after each stage if done in stages. Receipts within 1 year of applying; rebate within 12 weeks. Below-ground walls and slabs must be R20 or less before and gain at least R20.
basement.deadline: Receipts dated within 1 year of applying.

airSealing.program: Yukon home insulation and air sealing rebate
airSealing.amount: The total air sealing rebate is $5,000 per building when the building meets or exceeds the air sealing target.
airSealing.basis: All-or-nothing: paid only when the 1.5 ACH target is met.
airSealing.conditions: Existing residence (5 years or older). Energy assessment with an NRCan-registered advisor before applying and a follow-up assessment after the work ($50 each at the reduced fee), with a new assessment after each stage if done in stages. Receipts within 1 year of applying; rebate within 12 weeks. At least 3 air changes per hour at the first assessment and 1.5 or fewer afterwards, with an HRV installed.
airSealing.deadline: Receipts dated within 1 year of applying.

windows.amount: $120 per window to a maximum rebate of $1,800 per home or building.
windows.basis: $100 used because the page's own summary still says $100 per window and $1,000 maximum, while the body says $120 and $1,800.
windows.conditions: Complete ENERGY STAR-certified window assemblies (sealed glass units alone don't qualify); heated building at least five years old; rebate within 12 weeks.

ashp.amount: You can claim 50 per cent of project costs up to a maximum of $10,500.
ashp.conditions: Cold-climate air-source units on NRCan's list for Manitoba and Yukon (or ENERGY STAR ground-source); home at least six months old; existing non-electric heat kept as backup; electric systems kept and enrolled in Yukon Energy's Peak Smart Home; final electrical inspection report.

gshp.amount: You can claim 50 per cent of project costs up to a maximum of $10,500.
gshp.conditions: ENERGY STAR certified ground-source units; same conditions as air source.

thermostat.amount: 25 per cent of eligible costs up to $250 per home for applicants that are not enrolled in the Peak Smart Home program; 75 per cent up to $750 for enrolled applicants.
thermostat.conditions: Device bought after December 4, 2024 and eligible for Peak Smart Home; enrolment proof needed for the 75% rate.

measureNotes.doors: The window rebate page doesn't mention doors.
measureNotes.hpwh: No HPWH rebate; Yukon's hot-water rebates cover solar hot water and drain-water heat recovery.
measureNotes.assessment: Not a rebate: reduced-fee assessments cost "$50 for a pre-renovation assessment and $50 for a return visit".
